gbm_population_evidence.quote: Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma, IDH-Wildtype; Gliosarcoma; Recurrent Glioblastoma, IDH-Wildtype; Recurrent Gliosarcoma; Resectable Glioblastoma

candidate_evidence.quote: ERAS-801, an EGFR inhibitor that can penetrate the central nervous system, binds to the tumor cells that express EGFR and may help shrink or slow the growth of the tumor cells.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Patients must have histologically proven newly diagnosed WHO grade 4 glioblastoma/gliosarcoma
which is progressive or recurrent following radiation therapy +/- chemotherapy

tumour_pk_planned_evidence.quote: To evaluate the pharmacokinetic (PK) profile in plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and tumor tissue of ERAS-801 in recurrent glioblastomas.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: To evaluate the pharmacodynamic (PD) impact of ERAS-801 treatment in recurrent glioblastomas.

role_evidence.quote: EGFR Inhibitor ERAS-801 (other names: ERAS 801, ERAS-801, ERAS801): Given PO

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: EGFR inhibitor that binds to tumor cells expressing EGFR

role_evidence.quote: Fludeoxyglucose F-18 (other names: 18FDG, FDG, Fludeoxyglucose (18F), fludeoxyglucose F 18, Fludeoxyglucose F18, Fluorine-18 2-Fluoro-2-deoxy-D-Glucose, Fluorodeoxyglucose F18): Given FDG

source_quote.quote: Patient tumor sample must have wild type IDH with evidence of EGFR mutation/amplification by Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA)-certified laboratory assay.
Patient tumor sample must have wild type IDH with evidence of EGFR mutation/amplification by Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA)-certified laboratory assay.
Patient initial tumor sample must have wild type IDH with evidence of EGFR mutation/amplification by CLIA-certified laboratory assay.

coder_notes: Cohort B eligibility criteria are only given as 'Closed'; EGFR/IDH requirements listed for Cohorts A and C. Title states EGFR amplification or mutation for the trial. FDG is a registered intervention used for PET imaging (diagnostic) and its uptake is also a pharmacodynamic outcome.
